newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Former police enemies join forces in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Former police enemies join forces in Bosnia.

text.p: Bosnian Serb and Moslem-Croat Federation police have cooperated for the first time since the end of the war in a criminal investigation, leading to the arrest of two robbers, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday.

A Serb police chief in northeast Bosnia asked federation police to help when the armed men crossed former front lines after robbing a Serb family of 124,000 German marks ($73,000) and wounding one person near the town of Bijeljina.

Federation police arrested them in Tuzla, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Bijeljina and handed them over to the Serb police on the former confrontation line two days ago. About 30,000 German marks were also returned.
U.N. police spokesman Alexander Ivanko said: "This is an excellent example of cooperation. We hope this will become more a habit than an isolated event."
